dribtard for macOS
==================

The short version
-----------------

1. Drag "dribtard-mac.app" into your Applications folder.
2. Double-click "Fix and open.command" (the file next to this one).
   A Terminal window opens, fixes the app and launches it.
3. After that, double-click "dribtard-mac.app" as normal.

macOS refuses apps that were downloaded and are not notarised by Apple. The
helper does exactly what Apple's own "Open Anyway" does, in one step: it removes
the quarantine flag, restores the app's execute permission, signs the app on
your Mac, and opens it. It is safe to run again at any time.

It also fixes the "dribtard-mac.app is damaged and can't be opened" and
"cannot be opened" messages, which appear when a copy lost its execute
permission (for example, a zip made on Windows) or its signature no longer
matches the files.

If double-clicking the helper only shows "permission denied" or does nothing,
open Terminal and run this instead:

  sh "/Applications/Fix and open.command"

(Use the path where you put the helper if it is not in Applications.)


If you prefer to paste a command
--------------------------------

Open Terminal (Applications -> Utilities -> Terminal) and paste this one line,
then press Return:

  APP=$(ls -d ~/Downloads/dribtard-mac.app /Applications/dribtard-mac.app 2>/dev/null | head -1); if [ -z "$APP" ]; then echo "Move dribtard-mac.app into /Applications first"; else xattr -cr "$APP"; chmod -R u+rwX,go+rX "$APP"; chmod +x "$APP/Contents/MacOS/dribtard-mac"; codesign --force --deep --sign - "$APP"; open "$APP"; fi


Doing it without Terminal at all
--------------------------------

- Right-click (Control-click) the app and choose "Open".
- Or open System Settings -> Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, and click
  "Open Anyway" next to the message about dribtard-mac.

On macOS 15 and later the right-click shortcut is often missing, so "Open
Anyway", or the helper above, is the reliable path.

Do not launch the "dribtard-mac" file inside
dribtard-mac.app/Contents/MacOS by itself - always launch the .app.


First run
---------

The app is an accessory app: it has no Dock icon, just a floating panel.

macOS will ask for Accessibility permission (System Settings ->
Privacy & Security -> Accessibility). Turn dribtard on there. If the global
keys still do nothing, also turn it on under Input Monitoring.

The panel should then appear. If it does not, press the menu key, which is
the backslash key ( \ ) by default.
